summary: Roosevelt and Elliott idle at the club until four, then drive to the Lees, where their mother and sisters are staying. He is pleased that the two families get along so well.

events.detail: Breakfast and a lazy day at the club with Elliott
Visits the Lees, where his mother and sisters are guests

tr_quotes.text: The families get on beautifully together; and they are all just as lovely as possible.

headline: Tennis and singing at the Lees
summary: Roosevelt breakfasts with Elliott and brings him to the Lees for a day of tennis, walks and songs.

events.detail: A day at the Lees with Elliott: tennis, walks and singing

headline: Garden party at the Winthrops
summary: Roosevelt brings Elliott to dinner at the Lees, escorts Alice to the Winthrops' garden party and back under a bright moon, and then drives Elliott home.

events.detail: Dinner at the Lees with Elliott
Garden party at the Winthrops with Alice

headline: Charades and hide-and-seek in Salem
summary: A big party of Roosevelts, Lees, Saltonstalls and Peabodys has lunch at the Lee home in Salem, then drives over to the Peabodys to spend the night with dancing, charades and hide-and-seek.

events.detail: Large family excursion to Salem
Night at the Peabodys with dancing and games

headline: Ike Iselin comes to visit
summary: The party is back in Boston by morning, and Ike Iselin arrives to stay a few days, and Roosevelt takes him and Elliott to the D.K.E. theatricals and then to the club.

events.detail: Returns from Salem to Boston
Ike Iselin arrives for a visit
D.K.E. theatricals with Ike and Elliott

headline: Class Day in Hollis Hall
summary: On Class Day Roosevelt marches with his class in dress suits and silk hats, helps run the class spread in the gym and joins the exercises around the tree. That night he sits with Alice for nearly two hours in his old Hollis Hall room, looking down on the lantern-lit Yard, and gets to bed at four.

events.detail: Marches with his class to chapel and the theater
Oversees the class spread in the gymnasium
Joins the Class Day tree exercises
Watches the illuminated Yard with Alice from Hollis Hall
Supper at the Lanes, then the club

tr_quotes.text: At 8.15 I took possession of my darling, and had my reward.

uncertain: The record supplies the name Hollis Hall in brackets.

headline: Garden party at the Lowells
summary: After breakfast at the club, Roosevelt drives Jack Kingsford, Ike Iselin and Elliott to dinner at the Lees, followed by the Lowells' garden party.

events.detail: Drives friends and Elliott to dinner at the Lees
Garden party at the Lowells

headline: A stroll in the woods with Alice
summary: Roosevelt takes his visitors to Chestnut Hill by a roundabout route to show off the countryside. Iselin and Kingsford return to New York, and in the evening he and Alice take a lovely walk in the woods.

events.detail: Scenic drive to Chestnut Hill with his guests
Iselin and Kingsford go back to New York
Evening walk in the woods with Alice

tr_quotes.text: She grows sweeter and prettier every day

headline: A summer evening walk
summary: After a late breakfast Roosevelt brings Elliott to the Lees for the day, and in the evening he and Alice walk out in the cool summer air.

events.detail: Day at the Lees with Elliott
Evening walk with Alice

headline: Packing up four years
summary: While the others go to Nahant, Roosevelt stays behind to pack and settle his bills. He marvels that college is over but feels no gloom, with Alice beside him and only four months until their wedding.

events.detail: Packs up and pays his bills at the end of college
Reflects in his diary on finishing Harvard

tr_quotes.text: To think of the four years being over!
My cup of happiness is almost too full.

headline: Harvard graduate, magna cum laude
summary: Roosevelt receives his B.A. from Harvard magna cum laude, finishing 21st among 177 classmates, with John D. Long giving the main address. He spends the day at the club, attends the Dexters' garden party and drives Alice back to Chestnut Hill. Meanwhile Douglas Robinson is courting Conie and Elliott works at Uncle James Gracie's bank.

events.detail: Graduates from Harvard with a B.A., magna cum laude, 21st of 177
Commencement address by John D. Long
Garden party at the Dexters, then drives Alice home
Drives Elliott back to Cambridge

tr_quotes.text: Commencement Day. Received my degree; I actually am an alumnus!
